judged_text: The Salesforce refresh now unconditionally overwrites Credential.key with the token response, dropping any extra fields (e.g. previously stored metadata) that existed in the old key object. Previously the jsforce connection refreshed tokens internally without rewriting Credential.key; now every isCacheValid miss performs a fetch plus a prisma.credential.update that replaces the whole key JSON with only the schema fields plus the old refresh_token. If the stored key carried any additional persisted fields from earlier versions of the integration, they are silently removed on the first refresh after this deploys — a same-column repurposing (full key object → narrowed token object) with no backup of the prior value.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh logic does `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }}})`, where `accessTokenParsed.data` is constrained to `salesforceTokenSchema` (id, issued_at, instance_url, signature, access_token, scope, token_type). This overwrites the entire `Credential.key` JSON, preserving only those fields plus the old `refresh_token`, thereby dropping any other previously persisted fields that may have existed in `credential.key` (e.g., additional metadata). That is verifiable from the diff and constitutes potential silent data loss on refresh.
